script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Family
Theme: identity

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

EXT. SUBURBAN NEIGHBORHOOD - DAY

A warm SUN shines over a quiet neighborhood. A house sits at the end of the street, with a sign in the front yard reading "The Smiths". The door creaks open, and out steps PETER SMITH, a 40-something man, dressed in a suit and tie, carrying a small bag.

INT. SMITH HOME - LIVING ROOM - DAY

Peter sets the bag down on the coffee table. His WIFE, JANE, a beautiful and elegant woman in her early 40s, looks up from her book with a quizzical expression.

JANE
Where have you been? You're late for dinner.

PETER
I'm sorry, dear. I had to stay late at the office. But I have good news. I've been offered a promotion.

Jane smiles, but there's a hint of sadness in her eyes.

JANE
That's wonderful, Peter. I'm so proud of you. But what about us? You've been working long hours for months now. We hardly see each other.

PETER
I know, Jane. It's been hard. But this promotion means more responsibility, more money, and a better future for our family.

Jane sighs, but Peter can see the doubt in her eyes.

JANE
And what about our son, Michael? He's growing up so fast. He needs his father.

INT. SMITH HOME - MICHAEL'S BEDROOM - NIGHT

MICHAEL SMITH, a 12-year-old boy with Peter's eyes and Jane's smile, lies in bed, staring at the ceiling. He hears his parents arguing downstairs.

MICHAEL (whispering to himself)
Who is Dad, really?

EXT. PARK - DAY

The following day, Peter takes Michael to the park. They sit on a bench, feeding the ducks.

MICHAEL
Dad, can I ask you something?

PETER
Of course, Michael. What's on your mind?

MICHAEL
Why do you work so much? You hardly ever come home.

Peter looks down, ashamed.

PETER
I want to give you and your mother a good life. A better life than I had growing up.

MICHAEL
But at what cost? You're missing out on our lives.

PETER
I know, Michael. I'm sorry. But I promise to make it up to you. I'll take more time off work, spend more time with you and your mother.

MICHAEL nods, but Peter can see the doubt in his eyes.

INT. SMITH HOME - KITCHEN - NIGHT

That evening, Peter cooks dinner for his family. They sit down at the table, and there's a newfound warmth in their interactions. Michael shares stories from school, and Jane talks about her day. Peter listens intently, fully present.

JANE
Dad, you've been amazing tonight. I'm so proud of you.

PETER
Thank you, Jane. And Michael, you're growing up to be an incredible young man. I'm so grateful for you both.

MICHAEL
Dad, can we do this more often?

PETER
Absolutely, Michael. We will.

INT. SMITH HOME - LIVING ROOM - DAY

A few weeks later, Peter receives an email on his laptop. It's a job offer from a competing company, offering him a higher salary and more responsibility. He looks up from the screen, torn.

PETER
(to himself)
Who am I, really? A provider, or a father?

He turns to Michael, who's playing a video game on the couch.

PETER
Michael, I have some news. I've been offered a job with a better salary and more responsibility. But I want to know what you think. Do you want me to take it?

MICHAEL looks up from the game, surprised.

MICHAEL
Can I have a say in this?

PETER
Of course, Michael. You're a part of this family too.

MICHAEL thinks for a moment, then smiles.

MICHAEL
Dad, I want you to be happy. And if this new job will make you happy, then you should take it. But promise me you'll still spend time with us.

PETER nods, relieved.

PETER
I promise, Michael. I'll make sure to balance my work and my family life.

MICHAEL nods, satisfied.

INT. SMITH HOME - LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

That evening, Peter sits on the couch, reading a book. Jane enters the room, carrying a cup of tea. She sits down next to him and takes his hand.

JANE
You know, Peter, I've always been proud of you. But I'm even more proud of you now. You're not just a provider, you're a loving husband and a dedicated father. And that's what really matters.

Peter looks into Jane's eyes, and for the first time in months, he feels truly fulfilled.

PETER
Thank you, Jane. I love you.

JANE
I love you too, Peter.

They share a long, loving embrace.

FADE OUT.

THE END
